title: Guitarist Bill Johnson
summary: Bill Johnson was a quiet, college-educated guitarist and singer from Kentucky who was already at the Nest and liked a drink.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Now, a member of the Russell band that's received perhaps the least amount of mention or fleshing out, so to

Yeah. Well, Bill was a nice guy. Nothing extemporaneous about him. I mean, he was just a quiet person. And he played guitar and did his job. Very well-schooled person. He was a college man or a college graduate. And he was very well-liked. There was nothin'... You know, he...
Was he there when you joined the bad the first...? I think he was, wasn't he? He was kind of already...

I think so. I think so. [CHILTON SAYS HE JOINED RUSSELL IN 1927] I think he was at the Nest Club when I first went down there. Yeah, the Nest Club, where Russell was the piano player. Yeah, Bill Johnson. He used to sing...
Where was he from? Do you know?

He was from Kentucky. Louisville or Lexington, one of those places -- Kentucky. [b. LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY, 1905] But he was brought up around Washington D.C. In fact, I think he was a graduate of Howard University. He was very well educated. And a nice person. Very quiet. I have to say nice... Never bothered nobody.
He used to sing with the band?
Yeah. He sang that number, 'You Might Get Better, But You Never Get Well.' He sang that. He sang a lot of numbers.

But he liked a little taste, too... Well, I guess everybody in the band did at that time. We were all young. Nobody was married at the time. Yeah, we all indulged a little bit. We weren't what you would call... We weren't lushes or anything like that. But we would always take a little drink, get a little spirit.
